summary: Salmon National Forest summit lookout near Salmon, staffed from 1912; abandoned 1942, ruins per two sites. No source describes the summit today.

facts.design: Small wooden lookout cab: 9 by 9 ft (1924 report) or 6 by 6 ft (1930s listing)
facts.status_note: Abandoned in 1942; two sites list ruins. A 1945 Coast and Geodetic Survey description calls the summit station a dilapidated shack. One site labels it Drive-Up (access type; no statement on public access). No source describes the summit today.

notes_for_editor: Sizes conflict (9x9 in 1924 per the Salmon Forest report and Bing Young; 6x6 in the 1930s per two sites); no source says whether they are one building. The record county Custer looks wrong (see corrections). The NGS survey mark QZ0558 (BALDY MTN LOOKOUT CABIN, 45 08 41 / 114 00 32) matches the record coordinates; its shack description is quoted only via Forest Lookouts and is credited to the Coast and Geodetic Survey, 1945 (corrected 2026-10-10; earlier note said undated). A 1967 obituary in the Recorder Herald calls its subject the first lookout on 'Bald Mountain, west of Salmon'; not used, because it does not clearly name this peak and it concerns a private person.
